name: Kong Shangren
bio: Kong Shangren (孔尚任, courtesy name Jizhong, 1648–1718) was a Qing-dynasty playwright and poet from Qufu in Shandong, a descendant of Confucius in the sixty-fourth generation. When the Kangxi emperor visited Qufu in 1684 on his southern tour, Kong lectured to him on the Classics, and he was soon given a post at the Imperial Academy in Beijing.

From 1686 he was sent to the Huai and Yangzhou region to oversee river works, and there he met survivors of the fallen Ming and gathered the memories that fed his best-known work, the chuanqi drama The Peach Blossom Fan (桃花扇), which he finished in 1699 after three drafts. He was dismissed from office in 1700, returned to Qufu and died there in 1718.
